questions.q: Which integration pattern is best suited to loading 10,000 legacy invoices once at go-live?
options: Real-time REST, one invoice at a time
questions.explain: Large one-time volumes fit the batch/bulk pattern best.

questions.q: What distinguishes an event-driven integration from a real-time REST integration?
options: In event-driven integration, Fusion announces something happened and a subscriber reacts, instead of a caller polling for changes
Event-driven integrations only run once a year
questions.explain: Event-driven flips the initiative: Fusion pushes a notification rather than being polled.

questions.q: Which of the four questions is NOT one used to decide an integration pattern in this lesson?
questions.explain: Volume, latency, direction, and frequency are the four deciding questions — not formatting.

questions.q: A vendor portal creates one invoice right now and needs it in Fusion immediately. Which pattern fits best?
questions.explain: A single record needed immediately fits the real-time REST pattern.

questions.q: Can the same underlying data (like AP invoices) be moved through more than one integration pattern depending on the scenario?
options: No, each data type is permanently locked to one pattern
Yes — the right pattern depends on volume, latency, direction, and frequency for that specific scenario
Only if the data is in XML format
questions.explain: The same data type can use different patterns depending on the specific requirement.
